title: Dimension of a field groupoid equals the dimension of its stabilizer
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with $U=\operatorname{Spec}K$ for a field $K$ [def-weil-field]. Here a groupoid means that these operations give a groupoid on all test-scheme points, naturally in the test scheme, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$ and composition $c$. Assume $s,t:R\to U$ are locally of finite type, tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $G=U\times_{\Delta_{U/S},\,U\times_SU,\,(s,t)}R$, the stabilizer algebraic space, with fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $\dim R=\dim G$. Dimension for an algebraic space means $\dim(X)=\sup_{x\in|X|}\dim_x(X)$, where $\dim_x(X)=\dim_v(V)$ for any etale scheme chart $V\to X$ and point $v$ over $x$; for a scheme, $\dim_v(V)$ is the infimum of the Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods of $v$.

source.place: Tag 06FF (lemma-groupoid-on-field-dimension-equal-stabilizer), in Situation situation-groupoid-on-field with B=S; dimension conventions: spaces-properties.tex, definition-dimension-at-point and definition-dimension.

proof.text: First record the chart calculation for $G$. For any affine etale chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to R$, write $a,b:K\to A$ for the maps induced by $s,t$. The pullback $W=V\times_R G$ is the equalizer of $s|_V,t|_V$. Choose an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset S$ containing the image of $U$; all the maps under consideration factor through it. The affine fibre-product formula gives $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{K\otimes_D K}K)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, where $I=(a(\lambda)-b(\lambda):\lambda\in K)$. A finite set generating $A$ as a $K$-algebra maps to generators of $A/I$. Thus $W\to U$ is of finite type. These $W\to G$ are an etale covering by base change. This proves the required chart test for $G\to U$: for any scheme chart $H\to G$, cover $H\times_G W$ by affine opens. Each maps etale to an affine $W$, hence is locally of finite type over $W$ (local finite presentation supplies finitely many generators), and composition gives local finite type over $K$. Descent through the resulting flat locally finitely presented surjective etale cover of $H$ gives that $H\to U$ is locally of finite type. The groupoid operations restrict to $G$, since arrows with equal source and target are closed under identities, inverse and composition. So $G$ is a group algebraic space locally of finite type over $K$.

Let $e_R\in|R|$ and $e_G\in|G|$ be the points of the identity. The constant-dimension lemma applied to $R$ and to the group groupoid of $G$ gives $\dim R=\dim_{e_R}R$ and $\dim G=\dim_{e_G}G$. Choose an affine etale chart $V\to R$ and $v\in V$ over $e_R$. Both maps $V\to U$ are locally of finite type by hypothesis, and are of finite type since $V$ is affine and $U$ has one point. Replace $V$ by its connected component $C$ containing $v$. The finite-type component lemma, applied separately to each structural map, makes $C$ a nonempty connected open subscheme still of finite type for both structures. The restricted chart $C\to R$ is etale. Set $T=C_{\mathrm{red}}$. Reduction is a homeomorphism, so $T$ is nonempty and connected, and it is reduced. On affine opens its rings are quotients by the nilradical; images of finite sets of algebra generators show that the two maps $T\to U$ are locally of finite type.

Write $\rho_a,\rho_b:K\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for the source and target maps. Their composites with evaluation $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\to\kappa(v)$ agree: the field-valued point of $R$ at $v$ represents the identity point, so after passing to a common field extension it equals an identity arrow; the two structural maps there coincide, and injectivity of the field extension descends the equality to $\kappa(v)$. The scalar-field uniqueness lemma applies to the nonempty connected reduced scheme $T$ and its two locally finite type structures. It gives a common field $L=C_a=C_b\subseteq\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Evaluation restricted to $L$ is a unital map from a field to the field $\kappa(v)$, hence injective. For every $\lambda\in K$, both $\rho_a(\lambda),\rho_b(\lambda)$ lie in $L$ and have equal evaluations, so they are equal. The affine-target correspondence therefore gives $s|_T=t|_T$, and $T\to R$ factors through $G$.

Put $W=C\times_R G$. It is an etale scheme chart over $G$ by base change. On any affine open $D=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset C$, the calculation of step 1 gives $W\times_C D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$, with $J$ generated by source-minus-target scalar differences. Step 3 says every such generator maps to zero in $B/\sqrt{(0)}$, so $J\subseteq\sqrt{(0)}$. Every prime of $B$ therefore contains $J$; the quotient correspondence identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with exactly the same closed sets. These homeomorphisms agree on overlaps, so $W\to C$ is a homeomorphism. In particular there is a unique point $w$ over $v$. It maps to $e_G$: a test-scheme point of $G=U\times_{U\times_SU}R$ is a pair $(u,r)$ with $\Delta_{U/S}\circ u=(s,t)\circ r$, so $u=s\circ r$ and points of $G$ are determined by their images in $R$; hence two field points of $G$ whose images in $R$ agree after a common field extension already agree after it, and $w$, whose image in $R$ is $\varphi(v)=e_R$, the image of $e_G$, is the point $e_G$. Also $\dim_w W=\dim_v C$, since their open neighbourhoods and chains of irreducible closed subsets correspond. The chart convention for dimension now gives $\dim_{e_G}G=\dim_w W=\dim_v C=\dim_{e_R}R$. Together with step 2 this proves $\dim G=\dim R$.

lean.statement: theorem fieldGroupoid_dimension_eq_stabilizer {S : Scheme.{u}} (K : Type u) [Field K] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ S) (R : AlgebraicSpace S) (s t : R.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk b)) (e : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ R.obj.obj) (i : R.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (c : Limits.pullback s t ⟶ R.obj.obj) (hgroupoid : IsPresheafGroupoid s t e i c) (hs : ∀ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ R.obj.obj) (f : V ⟶ Over.mk b), IsEtale a → a ≫ s = yoneda.map f → LocallyOfFiniteType f.left) (ht : ∀ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ R.obj.obj) (f : V ⟶ Over.mk b), IsEtale a → a ≫ t = yoneda.map f → LocallyOfFiniteType f.left) : etaleDimension R.obj.obj = etaleDimension (groupoidStabilizer s t)
